events.text:
## Recommendation
- **Pier ratings for this week:** St. Joseph 1, South Haven 1 (inferred), Grand Haven 0, Muskegon 1 (inferred). Expect slow pier fishing everywhere.
- **Go to St. Joseph** if you're fishing from a pier. It has the most recent pier-specific salmon report, but even that was slow.
- **If you can, fish a boat instead.** Muskegon and Grand Haven boats were rated good (3) on Aug 16.
- **Pier tackle, if you go:** glow spoons or plugs, and nightcrawlers or shrimp for coho. Those are the only pier baits the reports mention.

## Why
- The pier reports are weak: Grand Haven's Aug 16 pier report was rated 0 (slow), and St. Joseph's Aug 9 pier report was rated 1 (below average).
- Water is warming, not upwelling: the buoy temperatures rose 4 to 9 F over the last week, and I'd expect that to keep salmon offshore and away from the piers.
- Past late Augusts look similar: pier reports in comparable water temperatures were rated 1 at St. Joseph and Grand Haven.

## Evidence
**Recent reports** (latest is Aug 16, six days old)
- Grand Haven, Aug 16 (pier): spoons and plugs, "Pier anglers who were casting spoons found the freshwater drum and salmon bite to be slow. … Glow spoons and plugs worked well." Rated 0.
- St. Joseph, Aug 9 (pier): nightcrawlers, "Pier fishing was a little on the slow side… a few coho caught while using night crawlers." Rated 1.
- Grand Haven, Aug 2 (pier): "A few salmon were caught on glow plugs." Rated 1.
- South Haven and Muskegon: no pier reports in the last four weeks. Their ratings above are my inference from the neighboring ports.
- Boats did better: Muskegon, Aug 16, "a good mix of Chinook and coho salmon 30 to 80 down in 50 to 120 feet of water," rated 3. South Haven, Aug 16, "Salmon and trout were caught in 80 to 100 feet of water," rated 3.

**Past seasons** (history, similar water temperature, same time of year)
- St. Joseph, Aug 17, 2022 (pier): "There were a few Chinook caught but it was mostly all steelhead," rated 1.
- Grand Haven, Aug 24, 2022 (pier): "the action was slow overall," rated 1.

**Conditions now** (the tool returned a backtest summary for the week before Aug 22, not live data)
- Buoy surface water averaged 65 to 71 F, rising 4 to 9 F over the week at each port.
- No modeled pierhead temperatures, cold-layer depth, or wind forecast came back, so I can't check for an upwelling setup.

## Caveats
- The newest report is six days old, and the conditions data is a week-old summary, not live.
- Ratings for South Haven and Muskegon are inferred from neighboring ports, since neither has a recent pier report.
- General guidance (Michigan Sea Grant): north or east winds can push cold water toward the piers. A sharp drop in buoy temperature signals that happening. The last week showed warming, not a drop.

- Aug 9: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/369e344
- Aug 2: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/368a51e
- Historical, Aug 24, 2022: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3298204
- Historical, Aug 17, 2022: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3288194
